situation:
You are the guest experience manager for STONE ROW CHEESESTEAKS, a cheesesteak and hoagie chain of twenty-two stores. The owner (judge) is the third generation of the family to run it, and the grandparents' first shop still opens at six every morning for breakfast.

Breakfast has lost money for six straight quarters. The loyalty database shows morning orders at a small fraction of lunch, and the labor to open four hours early costs more than those orders bring in. On the numbers alone, ending breakfast and opening at ten-thirty would stop the loss.

Long-tenured store managers disagree. They say the morning regulars are construction crews working nearby, that those crews order twenty sandwiches at lunch on the same day they buy coffee at six, and that they will buy both somewhere else if the doors are shut. The database records each order separately and cannot tell whether the same guest came back at noon.

Ending breakfast at all twenty-two stores stops the loss immediately, but it may take the crews' lunch business with it and it closes a routine three generations of regulars have kept. Keeping breakfast only at the stores near job sites, and tagging loyalty accounts for a quarter to see who returns, keeps the loss running and gives twenty-two stores two different opening times to explain.

The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend one of the two and to say how the decision should be carried to the morning regulars and to the store managers, and through which local media. The owner (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions, and will thank you when you have finished.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of STONE ROW CHEESESTEAKS. Business background is the same as the situation above. You are the third generation to run the chain, breakfast has lost money for six straight quarters, and the store managers who have been with you longest read the morning very differently than the loyalty database does.

You want the guest experience manager to recommend either ending breakfast at all twenty-two stores or keeping it only at the stores near job sites while tagging loyalty accounts for a quarter, and to tell you how the decision reaches the morning regulars and the store managers.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: If we do the opposite of what you recommend, what does it cost us?
What do we tell the managers who see it differently?
